howto.goal: Capture all of the other side's pieces, or leave them with no legal move.
howto.setup: English checkers on an 8 by 8 board. Each side starts with twelve pieces on the dark squares. White moves first.

sections.title: Moving
sections.text: Pieces move one square diagonally forward. Captures are compulsory: if you can jump, you must.

sections.title: Jumping
sections.text: Jump over an adjacent enemy piece to an empty square beyond it, and that piece is removed.

sections.title: Kings
sections.text: A piece reaching the far rank becomes a king and may move diagonally both ways.

sections.title: Draws
sections.text: 80 moves with no capture and no crowning is a draw.

controls: Click a piece, then the square to move to.
The ringed squares are the moves this lesson wants.
If several jumps are possible, any of them is legal.

frames.say: A piece on the far rank becomes a king.

demo.intro: The computer plays both sides. Watch how a forced capture changes the position.

lines.say: White and black face each other along the middle.
White steps forward on the left.
Black jumps over a white piece and captures it.

demo.outro: Captures are compulsory, so a piece offered up can force your opponent's reply.

steps.say: Click a piece that can move forward diagonally.
If a capture is shown, you must take it — click the piece, then the landing square.
Keep your back row intact so the other side cannot crown a king quickly.
Trade pieces when you are ahead: fewer pieces means fewer ways to lose.
